feat(projection): let a repository ask for a kernel instead of a full projection (S38, ADR-073)

The budget ADR-072 added was a ceiling nothing could get under. Kernel mode
is the way under it: keep the rules a reader cannot do without, the ones a
hard constraint or a command depends on, and defer the rest behind a section
that names each one and the command that shows it. A Python fixture projects
16% smaller, and nothing disappears silently -- a deferred rule is named in
AGENTS.md with simt rules show <id>, so the reader who needs one can get it.

full stays the default. Nobody has measured whether the smaller projection
loses compliance, and plan 0003 puts that study in front of the change; a
tool that made the trade silently would be deciding it on the reader's
behalf, which is the failure this package exists to prevent.

The classes are a closed vocabulary, and an unstated class defers rather
than packs. That asymmetry is deliberate: wrongly keeping a line defeats the
mode, wrongly dropping one costs a convention that rules show brings back.

The budget finding now takes the mode, because the two need different advice.
In full mode the projection is waiting to be trimmed; in kernel mode it has
already been trimmed, and an over-budget kernel is not a projection waiting
to be trimmed at all.
